Definition: from G2302; to expose as a spectacle:--make a gazing stock.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, theatrízō is the word for to make a public spectacle of. In Hebrews 10:33, Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions.
TheologicalSignificance: Believers made a public spectacle for their faith remind me that shame borne for Christ is not wasted, even when the crowd is watching.
